what_the_lease_was_used_for.deviation_from_the_grant_and_why: The grant named one figure; the change moved five, and all five had to move or the suite would be red. Converting the three routes to capability_gated takes them out of the legacy set, so legacyRoutes fell 51 to 48; adding the two named capability gates removes two of the four noSourceGuardMethods, so that fell 4 to 2; and declaring the invite route as a registered non-user principal (public_share_token) makes it the one method that cannot be compared against a guard in the source, so nonSourceComparableClasses rose 0 to 1. Recording the deviation is the point: the alternative was a half-moved set, and the direction of every movement is a measurement of real code, observed in both directions by negative controls.

what_the_lease_was_used_for.why_the_harness_and_the_boundaries_had_t: The harness IS the baseline, and routesWithoutResourceBoundary is machine-enforced from two opposite directions: the registry's own none_recorded set, and the separate assertion that routeFiles minus routesWithoutResourceBoundary is the number of routes whose verifiedAt and boundBy markers are present in real source. Control D, with the three registry entries reverted to none_recorded and the routes and harness figures left as landed, went red on five tests including 'expected 243 to be 246', 'expected 51 to be 48' and the five harness errors naming the three routes. Control B, with route B reverted to git show 16fb834f, went red with '/api/admin/onboarding/enhanced-invite shareToken: expected false to be true'.
what_the_lease_was_used_for.the_ceiling_was_lowered_after_a_measurem: scripts/ci/admin-route-registry-baseline.json legacyRouteLimit went 51 to 48. The true count was measured first and independently twice: the checker's own count and the proof test's exact-equality assertion, both at 48 while the ceiling was still 51, which is the state the checker reported as 'Legacy route classifications: 48/51'. Control D then drove the true count back to 51 and the checker failed with 'Legacy classification growth: 51 exceeds baseline ceiling 48', proving the ceiling is a live gate in this direction. Control D3 lowered the ceiling to 47 against a true 48 and the checker failed with 'Legacy classification growth: 48 exceeds baseline ceiling 47' while the proof test stayed 11/11 green, which is the sharper form of the point: the exact figure is pinned by the proof test, never by the ceiling.
